sections.html:
Two routes stand out: take a cash offer for the house exactly as it is, or list it and repair whatever a financed buyer's inspector flags. A lot of local housing was built during the postwar boom, which makes an as-is sale popular with owners unwilling to sink money into a house they are leaving.

Price is the catch. A listing may fetch more but brings repair requests, appraisal risk and a longer wait, while cash buyers pay less in exchange for speed. With either, insist on a written offer that names the closing date and says who pays title charges.

  • Find the deed, a payoff statement and the latest tax bill.
  • Write down known defects before anyone asks.
  • Note whether anyone is renting the house.

Haltom City lies along U.S. Highway 377, a few miles northeast of Fort Worth. The town took shape around World War II and grew fast: about 200 people in the late 1940s, 5,760 within roughly ten years, and 32,100 by the mid-1960s. The population was 39,018 in 2000.

Because the boom came after the war, many houses are now well past middle age, so ask a buyer or inspector early which systems need attention. Everything here is inside Tarrant County, giving you one county clerk and one appraisal district.

sections.h2: Short-term rental permit and hotel tax
sections.html:
A short-term rental has to register with the city for a permit before it can operate legally, and it must remit hotel occupancy tax as well. Under the city's definition, a short-term stay is under 30 consecutive days. Guests pay the tax; the owner or operator collects it and passes it along.

Haltom City hotel occupancy tax and short-term rental basics
RequirementHaltom City rule
Hotel occupancy tax rate7 percent
Stays coveredFewer than 30 consecutive days
Return and payment dueMonthly, by the last calendar day of the month after collection
Return with no revenueStill required
PermitAnnual short-term rental permit application with the city

An outside vendor processes the tax accounts and runs a support line for login credentials. Short-term rentals receive no exemptions. If the house has been rented this way, hand the buyer its permit and filing history.

sections.h2: Filing the hotel tax step by step
sections.html:
Filing is monthly, and it applies even when a month brings no bookings. Payment is due by the final calendar day of the month after collection, and penalties accrue afterward. A new operator asks the vendor's support center by phone or email for login credentials, then files and pays online, by phone or with a mailed check.

Exemptions are narrow. They cover permanent residents who stay at least thirty consecutive days, federal government business paid directly by the United States, and state government business paid directly by Texas, including public schools and political subdivisions. Nonprofits and charities are exempt from sales tax but not from this tax.

The state comptroller collects sales tax for the state, city and county, while the city collects hotel occupancy tax under its own ordinances. For permit questions, visit planning and community development at City Hall. Its hours run Monday through Thursday, and it is closed the rest of the week.

Haltom City appraisals and exemptions run through the Tarrant Appraisal District, which serves seventy-three taxing units across the county. Every unit picks its own rate using the district's values. Nobody should charge you to file an exemption.

The calendar runs like this: values lock January 1, homestead notices arrive around April 1, rates are adopted by late September, and bills land near October 1. Eligible owners may pay in two halves, the first by November 30 and the second by the following June 30.

Delinquency adds up quickly. From February 1 a six percent penalty and one percent interest begin, the penalty climbs each month through July 1, and an attorney fee may come later. A residence homestead may qualify for a payment plan of up to 36 months with some collectors.

  • Keep paying the undisputed portion during any appraisal appeal.
  • The lien stays with the house, so the title company pays any unpaid year out of your proceeds.
  • Ask the county tax office for a current balance before you sign.

sections.h2: How to look up and contest an appraisal
sections.html:
On the Tarrant Appraisal District website you will find a property search, a protest hearing search and an exemptions page. The district keeps a legacy site and a new site running side by side, so start from the links on its home page and skip old bookmarks.

Think the value is too high? File a protest inside the window printed on your notice, and collect photos and repair estimates showing the house's condition. A dispute that outlasts the review board continues to district court or arbitration. Keep paying the undisputed tax meanwhile.

sections.h2: Relief for older, disabled and military-service owners
sections.html:
Homeowners who are older or disabled receive an extra school exemption and a ceiling on school tax, set at the first qualifying year's amount. The ceiling can follow you in proportion to a new Texas homestead, and a surviving spouse aged 55 or more may keep it.

An owner with a service-connected disability receives an exemption that grows with the rating, and a 100 percent rating supports a total exemption on a residence homestead. Planning to buy again in Texas? Ask the district before closing how your ceiling would carry over. Homestead applications generally must reach the district before May 1.

sections.h2: Preparing a former rental or occupied house
sections.html:
If the house has been a short-term rental, wind down the accounts before closing. File every monthly return, including any with no income, and keep the confirmations. A buyer or title company that finds an unfiled month may ask you to resolve it before funds are released.

If a long-term tenant lives there, gather the lease, the deposit record and any repair requests. Tell each buyer whether the tenant will stay or leave, and by when. An investor may be glad to take over a lease, while a buyer who wants to move in will need the house vacant at closing.

sections.h2: What happens after you accept an offer
sections.html:
A title company takes over: it verifies ownership, collects payoff statements from your lenders and checks taxes. Next it drafts the deed and a settlement statement for you to read.

Signing happens before a notary. Once the deed is recorded, loans, taxes and closing charges are paid and the remainder goes to you. Cash deals skip the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the date holds more easily. Mention a tenant, or a need for extra moving days, as early as you can. Walk through the house a final time before closing and take photos of its condition, so any later question about what was left behind has a record.

faqs.q: Does Haltom City charge hotel occupancy tax on short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. Stays under 30 consecutive days carry a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax, which the owner collects and remits to the city each month.

faqs.q: Who appraises houses in Haltom City?
faqs.a: The Tarrant Appraisal District, which also serves the county's other taxing units.

faqs.q: What are the penalties if I miss my Haltom City property tax deadline?
faqs.a: A balance left on February 1 draws a six percent penalty plus one percent interest, and the penalty keeps rising each month until July 1.

faqs.q: Who must file a Haltom City hotel tax return?
faqs.a: Every hotel or short-term rental operator, each month, including months with no income. The deadline is the last day of the month after collection.

faqs.q: Is a nonprofit exempt from Haltom City hotel occupancy tax?
faqs.a: No. Only permanent residents of 30 days or more and certain federal and state government stays are exempt.
